files: packages/engine-core/scripts/p263-envelope-outcome-apply.mts — the heartbeat, the reversal's scope, the lease report, the refused-run artifact
changeUnderTest.notTouched: the census, the shared classifier (`envelope-outcome-movement.ts`), the blast-radius cap (`writer-blast-radius-guard.mjs`), the census digest, the county set (`p263-phase0-counties.mjs`) and the journal shape (migration 018). `git diff --name-only` names exactly the two files above.
changeUnderTest.whereTheHeartbeatSits: the FIRST statement of every batch transaction, on that transaction, before the journal INSERT and before the body UPDATE; one clock reading per batch serves both `applied_at` and the heartbeat.
changeUnderTest.reversalLeaseRule: the same `(write, buildable-envelope, <fips>)` scope, per batch, released before the next scope is taken; without `--county`, one scope per county the JOURNAL names.

falsifierResults.id: P-365 F1 — lease EXPIRED between batches
falsifierResults.withTheChange: The second batch refuses with `P263_LEASE_LOST`; the moved-atom set is exactly `${COUNTY}:1` and the journal holds exactly one row — the refused batch wrote and recorded NOTHING, and batch 1 stays journalled and reversible.
falsifierResults.preChange: `refusedWith: null`, `movedAtoms: [48021:1, 48021:2, 48021:3, 48021:4]`, `journalRows: 4`. The old code wrote ALL FOUR batches and journalled all four after the lease had expired. This is the dispatch's defect, reproduced in the old code's own writing.
falsifierResults.howTheClockIsDriven: an injected `now` (never a sleep): the take, then each batch, reads it in order.

falsifierResults.id: P-365 F2 — lease STOLEN by another holder between batches
falsifierResults.withTheChange: The later batch refuses with `P263_LEASE_LOST` and writes nothing; the batches already written stay journalled.
falsifierResults.preChange: `refusedWith: "ATOMS_WRITER_LEASE_NOT_HELD"`, `movedAtoms: [48021:1..4]`, `journalRows: 4` — all four batches written, and the theft surfaced only from the run's own RELEASE, after the writes it should have prevented.
falsifierResults.howTheftIsSimulated: a temporary BEFORE UPDATE trigger on the fixture's `atoms` table that steals the scope on the batch boundary the test controls — so the theft happens at a point in the run rather than at a time the test hopes for.

falsifierResults.id: P-365 F3 — a run whose batches OUTLAST the TTL (the inverse falsifier)
falsifierResults.withTheChange: The run COMPLETES: `heartbeats` equals the batch count and `lastExpires` is after the last write, so the renewal is a measurement rather than an assurance. This is the falsifier against the opposite error — a fix that refuses long runs instead of extending them.
falsifierResults.preChange: `result.lease` is `undefined`: the old code returned `{moved, journalRows, batches}` and reported nothing about the lease, so even a healthy run's renewal cannot be read off the artifact.
falsifierResults.clock: driven (`STEP_MS` per batch, with `2 * STEP_MS >= TTL_MS` asserted so the run provably outlasts the TTL); nothing sleeps.

falsifierResults.id: P-365 F4a — a REVERSAL while another holder holds the county's scope
falsifierResults.withTheChange: The reversal refuses with `ATOMS_WRITER_LEASE_HELD_BY_OTHER` (from the take, since it now takes one), the stored state is unchanged, and all four journal rows remain unreversed — nothing was restored and nothing was marked.
falsifierResults.preChange: `refusedWith: null`, `storedStateUnchanged: false`, `unreversedRows: 0` — the reversal restored every atom and marked every row while another holder held `buildable-envelope:48021`.

falsifierResults.id: P-365 F5 — a two-county reversal, one scope per county the journal names
falsifierResults.withTheChange: `reversed: 5`, `batches: 5`, and `leases` names exactly `buildable-envelope:48021` and `buildable-envelope:48209` — one scope per county the journal names, each with its own heartbeat count and last expiry; the fixture is restored byte-identically.
falsifierResults.preChange: `result.leases` is empty/absent: the old reversal took no scope and reported none.

falsifierResults.id: O1-owned — the heartbeat is on the BATCH's transaction
falsifierResults.verdict: READ AT SOURCE (not falsifiable by a driven clock)
falsifierResults.evidence: `lockAndHeartbeatLease(txn, lease, {now})` is called inside `sql.begin(async (txn) => ...)`, before the journal INSERT and before the body UPDATE, on both the apply and the reversal path. A driven clock cannot distinguish 'same transaction' from 'separate connection', so this is stated as a reading rather than dressed as a measurement.

falsifierResults.id: O3-owned — a refused run ACCOUNTS for what it wrote
falsifierResults.evidence: The refusal carries `batchesWritten`, `atomsWrittenBeforeRefusal` and `journalRowsBeforeRefusal`, and the CLI catches `P263_LEASE_LOST` and writes an artifact with mode `APPLY-REFUSED-LEASE-LOST` / `REVERSE-REFUSED-LEASE-LOST` and exit 1. Gap named honestly: the CLI's refused-artifact path is NOT covered by a test in this lane — the fixture tests call the exported core, which returns the report rather than writing a file.

falsifierResults.id: O4-owned — this row changes WHEN, not WHAT
falsifierResults.evidence: `git diff --stat` names two files, neither of them the census, the classifier, the cap, the digest, the county set or migration 018. The dry-run digest is computed from the census buckets and none of that arithmetic is in the diff, which is what lets the dispatch's expectation stand: Williamson's fresh dry run must still reproduce `e53c197f…67f`.

artifactShapeAfterThisChange.apply: `lease: {taken, runId, holderLabel, scope:{scopeType,scopeId}, heartbeats, lastExpires, released, releaseReason, releaseFailure, refusal}` — `refusal` is null on a clean run and carries the code, the storage cause, the message and the counts written before it on a refused one. `taken: false` when there was nothing to write.
artifactShapeAfterThisChange.reverse: `leases: [ ...same shape, one per county scope... ]`, plus `reversed` and `batches` as before.
artifactShapeAfterThisChange.refusedRuns: `mode: "APPLY-REFUSED-LEASE-LOST" | "REVERSE-REFUSED-LEASE-LOST"` with `writes.refused: true` and the counts; exit 1; the artifact is still written so a refused job leaves a record.
artifactShapeAfterThisChange.whyThisIsTheMeasurement: `heartbeats` and `lastExpires` are what turn 'the lease was held for the whole run' into something a record can show: a run that took a lease and never renewed it reports `heartbeats: 0` and a `lastExpires` that predates its own last write, whatever its prose says. For Williamson's apply the integration seat should expect `heartbeats >= batches` and `lastExpires` after the last write.

changesThisCheckpoint: packages/engine-core/scripts/p263-envelope-outcome-apply.mts — `lockAndHeartbeatLease` as the first statement of every batch transaction in `applyCountyMovement`; the same for each county scope in `reverseMovementRun`; `LeaseRunReport` + `leaseReportOf` + `releaseAfterRun` + `leaseRefusalRecord`; the `lease`/`leases` artifact fields; the two REFUSED-LEASE-LOST artifact modes; the docstring's new 'THE LEASE, HELD FOR AS LONG AS IT WRITES (P-365)' section and the reversal's lease rule.

packages/engine-core/scripts/__tests__/p263-envelope-outcome-apply.integration.test.mts — the five P-365 falsifiers and the helpers that drive them (an injected clock, a lease-stealing trigger, a multi-county journal).
whatIsNotDone: No store write, no `--apply`, no deploy, no merge: this lane is forbidden all four, and the fix's behaviour on a 32-minute county is therefore unmeasured WALL-CLOCK. What is measured is the mechanism (refusal on a lost lease, renewal on every batch, one scope per county on a reversal) against a real Postgres.

The CLI's refused-artifact path (the `APPLY-REFUSED-LEASE-LOST` / `REVERSE-REFUSED-LEASE-LOST` branches in `main()`) has no test in this lane. The CORE's refusal is tested; the file-writing wrapper around it is read-at-source.
Williamson 48491 remains held. This lane does not apply it; the integration seat rebuilds the image and reproduces dry run `dvt87` / digest `e53c197f…67f` before its apply.

`reverseMovementRun`'s multi-county path is exercised with two counties in the fixture; a real run-wide reversal of a five-county journal has not been performed (and must not be until the integration seat owns it).
